answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, a smart-contract bond is created for each identity, locking its own refundable bond. This makes it costly for multiple identities to participate. Only when cryptographic proof shows conflicting commitments signed for the same task, the slash is triggered. Like a glacier slowly eroding, this mechanism gradually eliminates malicious actors. In a secure system, identities can flourish like an oasis, and their interactions can be facilitated from a virtual terrace, free from manipulation.
